MESA Core · v0.9.5

Retrieval

v0.9.5 source: docs/retrieval-and-graph.md

This guide has equivalent English and Turkish versions. The source sections behind this page are at the bottom.

Three signals, two on by default#

BM25 uses FTS5 passage/evidence text and scoped citation lookup. Vector compares compatible semantic representations and runs when an embedding model is enabled. The assertion lane considers predicate, subject, object/literal and evidence; its default fusion weight is 0.0, so it does not contribute unless you raise it. Authorized canonical ownership and eligibility are resolved before rank contribution.

Rank fusion, not a probability#

Runtime defaults: k=60, vector weight=8.0, BM25 weight=1.0, assertion weight=0.0, with one-based ranks. A zero lane weight removes that lane’s fusion contribution. The calculator deliberately uses unit weights as a teaching example. A duplicate hit casts one lane vote. RRF(c)=Σ w/(k+rank). Lane-local citation boosts change lane order, not RRF increments. A separate query-dependent legal factor follows fusion. See the retrieval explanation for the exact distinction and an illustrative calculator.

Context limits#

Context defaults to a 2048-token formatted-evidence budget and single search. Optional adaptive mode uses at most one planner call and two additional searches without widening scope.

v0.9.5 operation#

With models off, BM25 still retrieves stored source text. A disabled or incomplete vector lane is reported in degraded_sources; enabling embeddings backfills skipped vectors at startup. BM25 matches query tokens of 6 or more non-digit characters by their first 5 characters; shorter tokens and tokens with digits stay exact. Equal scores break by stable content identity, so two fresh stores built from the same corpus rank identically. LanceDB 0.41 prefilters vectors by tenant, dataset and agent, and MESA verifies each candidate against SQLite before ranking.

Point-in-time search#

Pass a timezone-aware valid_at to search the revisions that were valid at that instant. Intervals are half-open: a revision matches when valid_from <= valid_at < valid_to, so at an exact amendment instant only the new revision matches. Searches without a date return active revisions only. Results include revision_number, valid_from and valid_to (empty strings when unset). See versioned documents.

Optional BGE reranking#

MESA_RERANK_ENABLED=false is the default. Enabling it needs the [ml] extra. MESA_RERANK_MODEL=BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 and MESA_RERANK_DEPTH=50 (range 1–50) configure the stage. The model loads lazily on first use, adding cold-start latency. After fusion, authorized full chunk texts are scored in a worker thread outside the shared search connection. Results add rerank_score; rrf_score and final_score retain their fusion values. Ties keep fused order.

Search indexes and scope cache#

Dataset-wide searches without a date or jurisdiction filter use the dataset's persistent FTS5 index, kept in step with commits inside SQLite transactions. Other scopes build a temporary FTS5 index containing only authorized rows; MESA_SEARCH_SCOPE_CACHE=true reuses it in a four-scope LRU until SQLite data changes. Every request still rechecks authorization.

Scoped legal identities and exact-match-first results#

With legal rules enabled, authorized titles and first-chunk law headers teach scope-cached law names, including K.. An exact law/article or decision’s own docket/decision reference can occupy at most three leading positions in document order after fusion and optional reranking; remaining results retain their order. A decision identity must start within the first 300 characters of chunk zero. Later quotations do not count. Court-name mentions such as AYM alone do not select the Constitution.

retrieval_provenance.legal_items returns versioned items with original chunk offsets; these are separate from SPO facts and do not add fusion score. MESA_LEGAL_RULES_ENABLED=false skips legal processing, hides stored legal annotations in result copies and leaves generic retrieval available. Existing snapshots/identities remain stored.

The sections of the upstream file that back this page, unchanged. Source section links open the appendix automatically.

Lanes and scoring#

MemoryDAO.search_v4_memory is the canonical search primitive. Tenant, dataset,

agent, committed-state, jurisdiction and temporal eligibility are checked

before candidate rank contribution. Physical vector IDs must agree with

canonical ownership/evidence.

LanceDB prefilters vectors by tenant, dataset and agent. MESA checks the

matching IDs against SQLite's authorized candidates before cosine ranking,

including any narrower time, jurisdiction or ownership constraints. It also

rechecks SQLite ownership when materializing results. A whole-table search

can skip the rank-time filter when MESA has verified every row in the pinned

LanceDB version. On startup, MESA fills

the scope column in older vector tables from SQLite and preserves the stored

embeddings. Live projection groups vector writes and keeps each mutation's

own durable receipt. LanceDB periodically compacts the resulting fragments.

BM25 uses a temporary FTS5 index containing only authorized assertions, so

out-of-scope rows do not enter its corpus statistics. The scope cache reuses

that index only while SQLite's data version matches the pinned read snapshot.

When a search's authorized corpus is exactly one dataset's active committed

chunks (single dataset, no temporal or jurisdiction filter, and the agent

scope excludes zero active committed rows), MESA uses that dataset's

persistent per-(tenant, dataset) FTS5 index maintained in the same SQLite

commit, supersession, rollback, and purge transactions (and rebuilt from

SQLite if missing). Persistent indexes are never shared across datasets or

tenants, and every narrower scope uses the per-query temporary FTS5 index.

The scope_audit describes eligibility; negative tests also check rank and

observable diagnostic isolation.

LaneCandidate signal
VectorCompatible ASSERTION_VECTOR semantic representation; query embedding
BM25FTS5 passage/evidence and lexical matching; scoped typed citation lookup
AssertionPredicate, subject, object/literal, evidence, token coverage and confidence

For candidate c, RRF(c) = Σ w_lane / (k + rank_lane(c)), with ranks starting

at 1 and default k=60. Runtime defaults are vector weight 8.0, BM25 weight

1.0, and assertion weight 0.0 (see the

dev benchmark).

Duplicate backend hits cast one vote. Ties use candidate identity. The RRF

helper in mesa_storage/retrieval_scope.py uses unit weights when none are

passed; the server passes its configuration to the DAO.

Lexical exact citation +200 and same-statute +40 change the BM25/lexical lane

ordering. Assertion exact citation +150 and same-statute +40 change assertion

ordering. These are not RRF score increments. After fusion a query-dependent

legal factor is applied: exact statute/article 1.5, same statute 1.25, competing

statute 0.25, otherwise 1.0. A query without recognized legal citations has

factor 1.0. HTTP/SDK final_score is final fused relevance; higher is better.

rrf_score, legal_factor and lane raw_score are separate diagnostics;

MCP response adapters may expose a normalized score field.

Optional reranking orders fused

candidates by a cross-encoder score after the search connection is released.

It adds rerank_score; rrf_score and final_score retain their fusion values.

Equal reranker scores retain fused order. Reranking is off by default.

Typed ingestion identity uses a bounded alias ontology and immutable provenance.

It improves scoped pre-rank candidate discovery, including article chunks with

little title context. Reserved caller metadata cannot opt into trusted identity.

This contract checks structural linkage; it cannot prove a producer attached

the correct law, revision or real-world interpretation.

Backend failure behavior#

SQLite owns canonical entities and assertions; LanceDB is the derived vector

projection. Responses expose bounded scope_audit and vector_lane

diagnostics. Their hashes identify contracts/config/scope, not a certification.

A configured operational backend failure yields explicit 503 rather than

silently claiming complete search. Custom embedding providers are configured

but non-operational until a successful embedding call.

Context and adaptive search#

GET /v4/sessions/{session_id}/context defaults to token_budget=2048 and

retrieval_mode=single. ContextBuilder packs evidence once using cl100k_base.

The budget applies to formatted model-visible context, not the entire HTTP

response. If canonical BPE cannot load, the current OpenAI counting path uses

one token per UTF-8 byte as a conservative offline upper bound, even when

strict=True is passed. This may pack less evidence and is not exact cl100k

measurement. Exceptions raised by the counting interface propagate.

Complete graph proof must fit atomically; compact proof retains canonical

supporting evidence and may omit optional structural details.

Adaptive mode plans only if Q0 is empty or no top-three candidate has two-lane

support. It sends only normalized query text to one planner call, accepts at

most two reformulations, rejects invented legal citations and reuses the original

scope. Outer query fusion uses Q0=1.0, Q1/Q2=0.5. query_fusion_score and

query_origins remain separate from lane provenance. Planner/expansion failure

preserves Q0. This mode does not generate an answer or certify model quality.

Interpreting examples#

For a neutral single-hop “archive hours” query, inspect source evidence and

mutation state. For a multi-hop query, require every supporting assertion in

the path; a reachable entity alone is insufficient. An empty result is a valid

no-evidence outcome, not proof that a statement is false. Version/date-sensitive

queries should supply timezone-qualified valid_at or an interval and, when

needed, jurisdiction. These are request patterns, not measured benchmark results.

Core context packing is distinct from the independently sealed Profile B

context and scorer in E2E Certification.

Round 14 dev benchmark#

Measured on 2026-11-01 using the frozen Tier M corpus: 141 documents and 5,041

chunks ingested through this branch's authenticated document endpoint, with

article chunking enabled, extraction off, embeddings and graph on. Only the

101-question dev split was evaluated (85 answerable, 16 no-answer); the test

split was not accessed. The unmodified mesa_eval.py computes passage hit@5

and MRR on answerable questions; latency covers all 101 questions. Retrieval

limit and reranker depth are both 50, with max_length 1024 for the reranker.

Embeddings use BAAI/bge-m3 (1024 dimensions, normalized), and reranking uses

BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3. Each row below uses the same complete store, GPU

models and other lane weights of 1. Model revisions, package versions, source

hashes, unrounded MRR and the selection rule are in

the measurement data.

Vector weightRerankerPassage hit@5Passage MRRSearch p50 (s)Search p95 (s)
1Off0.51760.39531.26932.0035
1On0.74120.68161.95482.5736
2Off0.57650.45651.27081.9640
2On0.75290.70551.95692.6364
4Off0.65880.51521.28361.9469
4On0.77650.70691.92792.6100
8Off0.67060.56631.28491.9115
8On0.76470.69731.91612.5360

The default is selected from reranker-off MRR because reranking is off by

default. Weight 8 has unrounded MRR 0.566347, versus 0.395339 at weight 1: a

gain of 0.171008, exceeding the required 0.02. The runtime default

is therefore 8.0. Without that gain the default would stay 1; ties use the

smaller weight. Weight 4 has the best reranker-on MRR in this sweep. Overrides

remain available through MESA_RRF_VECTOR_WEIGHT. These measurements describe

this Turkish legal corpus and these models; other corpora/models need their own

measurements.

A separate device pass at vector weight 1 measured the optional reranker:

Inference device / rerankerPassage hit@5Passage MRRSearch p50 (s)Search p95 (s)
GPU / Off0.51760.39531.25311.9953
GPU / On0.74120.68161.96272.6029
CPU / On0.74120.681626.915833.8756

Hardware: Colab A100-SXM4 40GB and Intel Xeon 2.20GHz CPU, with eight CPU

threads. Python 3.13.16, Torch 2.11.0+cu130, sentence-transformers 5.7.0,

transformers 5.21.0, NumPy 2.5.4, LanceDB 0.41.0 and Kùzu 0.11.3. These are

compatible installed Colab packages, rather than the lockfile's exact ML pins;

the local gate uses the locked dev environment. Both models were explicitly

acquired before runtime startup. The device pass moves both models to CPU

without quantization for its CPU row.

Requests use the actual authenticated HTTP route through ASGI, without TCP.

Passes run sequentially, reusing the store and caches; one first-query warmup

is excluded from each pass (warmup values are in the data). These are descriptive

latencies, including embedding, scoped retrieval and optional reranking, rather

than a controlled hardware speedup claim. The benchmark store was ingested with

the measured source commit and then reused after the search-lock change, which

kept all 101 dev top-50 result dictionaries identical. The original frozen

corpus and question files were read only throughout.
